packer.name: LZEXE
evidence: ASCII signature 'LZ91' at file offset 0x1c (28), the location e_lfarlc points to instead of a real relocation table
e_crlc == 0 in the outer MZ header (no relocations declared for the packed stub)
e_cparhdr == 2 (header is only 32 bytes, consistent with the minimal LZEXE stub header)
e_ip/e_cs == 0x000E / 0x1298 point into the LZEXE decompression stub, not the real game entry point

mz_header_outer.note: declared image size matches actual file size, as expected for an LZEXE-packed file (the packed stub + compressed body is itself a well-formed tiny MZ file)

files.version_strings: not yet extracted (next step now that unpacking is done)

unpacked.independent_cross_check: SHA1 matches an independently published UNLZEXE-decompressed DAVE.EXE (Internet Archive item 'Dangerous Dave (LZW decompressed)') byte-for-byte.

mz_header_unpacked.entry_bytes_disassemble_sane: mov dx,imm16; mov cs:[disp],dx; mov ah,30h; int 21h (DOS get-version) ... — confirms this is a real, sane program start, not garbage

files.initial_observation: First bytes decode as a sequence of little-endian 32-bit values (0x191, 0x648, 0x6c8, 0x748, 0x7c8, 0x848, 0x8c8, 0x948, ...) consistent with a resource/chunk offset table; entries after the first increment by a constant 0x80 (128 bytes) each.
files.tile_size_hypothesis: 128 bytes/chunk == 16 rows x 4 EGA bitplanes x 2 bytes/row, i.e. a 16x16-pixel, 4-bitplane (16-color) EGA planar tile. This is the standard EGA tile encoding and matches the observed constant stride exactly. Not yet confirmed by decoding actual pixel content — still a hypothesis pending a rendering check.
files.next_step: Decode a chunk under the 16x16x4bpp planar hypothesis and render it (or eyeball plane bit-patterns) to confirm it forms a coherent game tile rather than coincidental stride matching; cross-reference against any existing public Dangerous Dave format documentation.

notes: String extraction from build/DAVE_unpacked.exe found: '(C) 1990 SOFTDISK, INC.', 'BY JOHN ROMERO', and 'Turbo C++ - Copyright 1990 Borland Intl.' (this last one is the Turbo C++ runtime startup copyright string embedded by the linker, not an application string — see toolchain notes below).

This confirms: 1990 Softdisk-published Dangerous Dave, authored by John Romero, and gives strong direct evidence the toolchain is Borland Turbo C++ (likely v1.0 or v1.01, both copyright-dated 1990) rather than plain Turbo C.
Not yet determined: which specific episode/release this EXE corresponds to (shareware ep.1-only vs registered ep.1-3), or the exact Turbo C++ point version/patch.
This manifest must be updated, not silently replaced, if a version mismatch is later discovered.
